# `hs-run plan` — state map

<!-- generated by render_state_map.py — edit the SSOT, # learn: "${HARNESS_BIN_ROOT:-.}"/harness/data/hs-run-registry.d/<domain>.yaml, not this file -->

Every state `hs-run plan` can report, with what it means. Run the CLI, read the `state`, do the judgment that state names, run it again — each state is re-derived from artifacts on disk, so deleting an artifact regresses the state.

This file is generated. Change the source named in the comment above, then re-render with `render_state_map.py`; edits made here are lost on the next render.

## States that route something

The CLI hands these rule and reference paths over at the moment the step begins — the body does not repeat them.

| state | what it means | routes |
|---|---|---|
| `needs_scope_sizing` | The scaffold exists and nothing has sized it yet: does this fit in ONE plan? Asked here rather than after the phases, when the answer could no longer change anything. `--fast` declares the skip. | `plain-language-phrasing`, `references/multi-plan-split.md`, `references/grid-when.md` |
| `scope_needs_split` | The sizer judged this plan `multi` — too big for one plan. Split it, or record a written reason for keeping it whole; both are valid, silence is not. | `scope-and-contract-discipline`, `references/multi-plan-split.md` |
| `grid_needs_axes` | `--grid` is on and no axis receipt exists. Spawn `@grid-axis-selector`; it reads THIS plan's prose and writes the receipt. The step exists because a grid built on canned axis values lands mostly-N/A. | `references/grid-when.md` |
| `grid_needs_fill` | Axis receipt present, no fill source. Spawn `@grid-filler`; it writes cell content to a JSON file rather than editing the grid. | `references/grid-preregistration.md` |
| `grid_unresolved` | The coverage-grid exists but no cell carries real content. Either ground the cells or write the thin-grid attestation INTO the artifact. | `references/grid-mode.md` |
| `grid_needs_build` | Fill source present, no skeleton grid. Deterministic: run the one command the envelope prints. | `references/grid-coverage-step.md` |
| `grid_needs_expand` | Skeleton built. Validate the fill source, then relay it through the expander — the validation is what keeps unground cells honest stubs. | `references/grid-coverage-step.md` |
| `grid_needs_emit` | Grid filled, no coverage-grid artifact yet. Deterministic: run the one command the envelope prints. | `references/grid-coverage-step.md` |
| `approval_drifted` | The plan WAS validly approved, then the body changed. A stale approval, not a conflicting story: re-review the part that drifted. | `plannotator-review-gates` |
| `completed` | Terminal. The whole chain finished; what is left is archiving the plan directory. | `output-rendering`, `references/archive-workflow.md` |
| `handed_off_to_cook` | The plan is in_progress and cook owns it now. Nothing left in the plan domain — continue with `hs-run cook next`. | `tdd-discipline`, `workflow-handoffs`, `references/cook-handoff-flags.md` |
| `approved` | Terminal for the plan domain. Hand off to cook using the flags the plan was built with — `--grid` carries via frontmatter, no retyping. | `scope-and-contract-discipline`, `workflow-handoffs`, `references/cook-handoff-flags.md` |
| `rejected` | Terminal. The review rejected this plan — revise the body and phases against the recorded reason before asking again. | `plannotator-review-gates`, `scope-and-contract-discipline` |
| `approval_invalid` | An approval artifact exists but does not back THIS plan — wrong plan, or no longer valid. Re-review which verdict is now correct; never re-stamp. | `plannotator-review-gates` |
| `needs_research` | The plan body still carries TBD placeholders. Spawn `@researcher`, then `record researcher --out <file>`. `--fast` declares the skip. | `intake-and-interview-discipline`, `counting-discipline`, `sampled-rate-reporting`, `references/research-phase.md` |
| `needs_planner` | Content is there but `plan-graph.yaml` is missing or invalid. This is the design step: decompose into phases, then spawn `@planner` and record it. | `testability-triad`, `scope-and-contract-discipline`, `architectural-constraints`, `adr-trigger`, `references/phase-decomposition.md`, `references/constraint-scan.md`, `references/solution-design.md`, `references/five-hat-elaboration.md`, `docs/system-architecture.md`, `docs/code-standards.md` |
| `needs_redteam` | Content and plan-graph are on disk, no red-team report is. Run the Goodhart check and the 6-lens pre-mortem yourself first — those findings feed the `risks:` frontmatter at C/H/M/L — then spawn `@red-teamer`. `--in-place` falls back to an inline persona pass. After applying findings, sweep the plan for consistency: a finding applied in one phase and not the others leaves the plan disagreeing with itself. `--fast` declares the skip. | `plan-quality-goodhart-premortem`, `verification-mechanism`, `persistent-risk-register`, `sampled-rate-reporting`, `references/red-team-gate.md` |
| `needs_model_attestation` | Everything disk-provable is proven. What remains is not: the red-team disposition, the validate interview, the consistency sweep. Do them for real, then run the approval command the envelope prints. | `plan-quality-goodhart-premortem`, `observation-signal-emit`, `references/validate-gate.md`, `references/verification-roles.md` |
| `scaffolded` | `plan scaffold` just wrote the directory. Reported by the scaffold verb itself, carrying the projection's own next step. | `intake-and-interview-discipline`, `plain-language-phrasing`, `references/tdd-plan-mode.md`, `references/multi-plan-split.md` |
| `absent` | Queried by `plan graph`: no `plan-graph.yaml` at all. Not a fault on its own — a plan reaches this shape before the design step writes one. Where the run is actually blocked by it, `needs_planner` fires and carries the pointers. | `references/plan-graph-format.md` |
| `invalid` | Queried by `plan graph`: the sidecar parses, and node(s) declare no `post`. The names are listed in the reply; nothing downstream can order a node that never says what it unblocks. | `references/plan-graph-format.md` |
| `malformed` | Queried by `plan graph`: the sidecar is there and does not parse. Distinct from `absent` on purpose — that difference is read off the filesystem, never from the parser's wording, so this state survives a reworded error. | `references/plan-graph-format.md` |
| `waiting_on_model` | `plan prompt <role>` just handed out a subagent prompt. Spawn the agent, then feed its output back with `plan record <role> --out <file>`. | `orchestration-protocol`, `agent-operational-discipline` |
| `no_plan` | No plan directory exists yet — the run starts by scaffolding one. Do the understand interview FIRST; the 5-fact floor is invariant. If a discovery brief already exists, scaffold INTO its folder by passing that dir's `--id`/`--slug` — scaffolding beside it orphans the brief in a sibling folder with nothing to notice. | `intake-and-interview-discipline`, `docs/system-architecture.md`, `docs/code-standards.md`, `harness/LESSONS.md` |
| `multiple_plans` | More than one plan directory resolves. Ambiguity, not failure — name the target with `--plan <dir>` rather than guessing. | `references/multi-plan-split.md` |

## States that route nothing

Not a gap: each is fully served by the `next_action` line the envelope already carries, and needs no extra file to act on.

| state | what it means |
|---|---|
| `not_a_plan_dir` | The directory named on the command line is not a plan. Nothing was read or written; check the path before re-running. |
| `cancelled` | The plan was deliberately cancelled. Nothing for this domain to do, by design, until a human un-cancels it — a leftover approval does not revive it. |
| `state_conflict` | Frontmatter and the artifacts on disk tell different stories. STOP: find out which side is lying. Never pick one and carry on. |
| `unresolved` | A directory that is not a finished plan — `plan.md` missing, or present with no `phases/phase-*.md`. Half-scaffolded plan to finish, or stray dir to remove. |
| `error` | The invocation itself was wrong — missing flag, unknown role, unresolvable plan. Nothing was read or written; fix the command and re-run. |
| `ok` | Queried by `plan graph`: the sidecar parses and every node declares its `post`. Cycles, ordering hazards and parallel conflicts ride back as warnings — a clean parse is not the same claim as a sound graph. |
